sources.title: MediaStream Recording
sources.locator: §2.1-2.3 (constructor, MIME, events, start/stop/timeslice), §2.3 isTypeSupported, §6.1 resource exhaustion
sources.observed_operation: Opened the fixed dated report and inspected algorithm text and surrounding context.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: isTypeSupported=true signals format capability only and can still fail for resource reasons; unsupported constructor MIME throws NotSupportedError; the actual current MIME is exposed after start; timeslice events are queued after a UA minimum; all-track-ended stops recording; individual blobs need not be playable while the completed concatenation must be.
sources.applicability: Primary current working-draft API semantics for MediaRecorder lifecycle, negotiation, buffering, and assembly; not a browser/version support matrix.

sources.title: Media Capture and Streams
sources.locator: §4.3.1.2 track life-cycle and mute/unmute/ended behavior; §8 event summary; §9.1 Navigator Interface Extensions and §9.2 MediaDevices secure-context IDL; §10.1 MediaDevices getUserMedia; §13 permissions integration
sources.observed_operation: Opened fixed dated report; inspected secure-context IDL, permission rejection, track-end and devicechange algorithms.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Microphone-source end reasons beyond application stop are implementation-defined; external ending queues an ended event, while explicit track.stop() does not; permission failure rejects NotAllowedError; a muted or disabled track may yield silence; devicechange is an event on available-device-set changes and can be coalesced.
sources.applicability: Primary stream/permission lifecycle authority; use for app behavior and test design, with browser/OS observations still required.

sources.title: Web Audio API 1.1
sources.locator: §1.32 AudioWorklet; §2.6 rendering an audio graph and render quantum
sources.observed_operation: Opened fixed dated report; inspected worklet scope, rendering-thread operation, configurable quantum, and real-time callback budget context.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: AudioWorkletProcessor runs in an audio rendering scope/thread; default render quantum is 128 frames but render size is configurable; work must meet real-time callback deadlines. The API supplies audio frames, not a finished encoded file/container.
sources.applicability: Primary design input for the custom processing alternative; exact browser worklet behavior and encoder/mux support remain test items.

sources.title: Chrome Stable Channel Update for Desktop
sources.locator: Stable Channel Update for Desktop heading/date and build line; official October 2026 archive search result
sources.observed_operation: Searched official Chrome Releases and read the matching 2026-10-06 desktop Stable result; direct archive open was throttled.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Version identifies the stable target announced by the release channel; rollout may occur over days/weeks, so test must record the installed full build rather than assume all users have it.
sources.applicability: Version anchor for the proposed Chrome validation matrix only; release note does not establish MediaRecorder format support.

sources.title: WebKit Features in Safari 18.4
sources.released_version_or_commit: WebKit release notes for Safari 18.4, published 2025-03-31
sources.observed_operation: Opened release article and read Media section and platform qualifiers.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Safari 18.4 release article describes WebM recording with Opus and ALAC/PCM audio tracks; its examples and wording do not specify a complete standalone audio-only MIME matrix. Ogg Opus/Vorbis is explicitly scoped to macOS Sequoia 15.4, iOS/iPadOS 18.4, and visionOS 2.4.
sources.applicability: Historical release evidence that Safari capability changed materially; candidate source for runtime probes only. Do not infer exact audio-only MIME strings or Safari 26 behavior from this paragraph.

sources.title: WebKit Features in Safari 26.0 and Apple Safari 26.0 Release Notes
sources.released_version_or_commit: Safari 26.0 feature announcement, 2025-09-15; Apple release note build 26 (20622.1.22)
sources.locator: WebKit Media section, lines 349-359; Apple Developer Safari 26.0 Release Notes, Media > New Features
sources.observed_operation: Opened WebKit article and Apple release-note search result; read the announced MIME example and release build metadata.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Safari 26.0 adds ALAC and PCM audio in MediaRecorder; example is audio/mp4; codecs=alac. The article does not specify an exact PCM MIME string or guarantee every combination on every OS/hardware configuration.
sources.applicability: Current Safari version and released capability anchor; probe exact MIME on tested desktop Safari and separately test playback/export.

sources.title: Safari Technology Preview 110 release notes
sources.locator: WebRTC > MediaRecorder fixes, lines 19-23; listed changesets r263511/r263633/r263891 and r263565/r263651/r263892
sources.observed_operation: Opened historical release notes and inspected the explicit regression-fix entries.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Release notes fixed an empty stopRecorder Blob after first use and start() ignoring timeslice in that old STP range.
sources.applicability: Historical regression/fix detail for proposing lifecycle and timeslice regression tests; says nothing by itself about current Safari 26 behavior.

sources.title: Chromium MediaRecorder handler source
sources.released_version_or_commit: Immutable Chromium source commit 19646947eb735f84c5ae91af1fe901273d67d4f7, authored 2025-09-04; not mapped here to Chrome 155
sources.locator: AudioStringToCodecId(), CanSupportAudioType(), and MIME validation/codec branches in media_recorder_handler.cc

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The source snapshot recognizes audio/webm and audio/mp4, maps Opus and PCM, and maps mp4a.40.2 AAC only under USE_PROPRIETARY_CODECS.

sources.title: extendable-media-recorder README
sources.released_version_or_commit: Mutable master README as retrieved 2026-10-10; exact commit and current npm version not exposed in retrieved view
sources.locator: README: Usage, Using a custom encoder, Setting the sample rate, Inner Workings
sources.observed_operation: Opened repository README; compared native path and custom encoder backend notes.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: README says it uses native MediaRecorder when possible; custom audio encoders are supported; Chrome's custom path consumes MediaRecorder WebM/PCM and parses EBML, while other browsers use Web Audio PCM.
sources.applicability: Architecture analog only; mutable docs and unpinned library do not establish current browser support or justify selecting the dependency.

sources.title: extendable-media-recorder issue 263: timeslice / requestData

sources.locator: Issue discussion and maintainer closure comment, especially discussion of WAV length metadata and requestData

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For that WAV encoder, the maintainer reported using a maximum/sentinel file-size value for timesliced WAV output and said requestData() remained unimplemented at closure.

sources.title: extendable-media-recorder issue 692: doubled WAV speed / timeslice report
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2025-08-08; closed status shown; library version and resolution commit unknown in retrieved page
sources.locator: Issue summary, environment fields, reproduction, and closure state
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue and inspected symptom, example, environment, and visible activity; no maintainer resolution was exposed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter describes audio/wav playback near 2x and dataavailable intervals near twice the requested chunk interval; version is unfilled and environment examples are not confirmed facts.
sources.applicability: Library-specific uncertainty that motivates WAV sample-rate/header and event-timing checks; no inference about native browser behavior or verified fix.

sources.title: High Resolution Time
sources.observed_operation: Opened the fixed dated report and inspected monotonic-clock and background-throttling conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Performance.now values with the same time origin use a monotonic clock and do not decrease with system-clock changes; in backgrounded tabs the user agent may throttle timers and periodic callbacks or freeze them entirely, without affecting monotonic-clock accuracy.
sources.applicability: Primary timekeeping basis for elapsed active-time accounting; proves a reliable clock source, not that a scheduled stop callback runs at its deadline.

sources.title: HTML Standard — Page visibility
sources.released_version_or_commit: HTML Living Standard, last updated 2026-10-09; mutable living document
sources.locator: §6.2 Page visibility: system visibility state update and visibilitychange event steps
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Page Visibility section of the current Living Standard and read the state, queued task, and event sequence.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The user agent determines system visibility; on change it queues a global task to update document visibility, then fires visibilitychange. Hidden/visible therefore signals a user-agent determination and handler execution is task-queued.
sources.applicability: Supports stop-on-hidden behavior as a signal-driven policy, not an instantaneous or hard real-time guarantee; exact Chrome/Safari behavior must be exercised.
